claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The augmented-coding workflow uses plan.md as the intent artifact: the agent is told to follow plan.md, take the next unmarked test, implement the test, and write only enough code to make it pass.
claims.quote: Always follow the instructions in plan.md. When I say "go", find the next unmarked test in plan.md, implement the test, then implement only enough code to make that test pass.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Augmented coding is defined as caring about code quality, complexity, tests, and coverage, in contrast to vibe coding, which cares only about system behavior.
claims.quote: In vibe coding you don't care about the code, just the behavior of the system. If there's an error, you feed it back into the genie in hopes of a good enough fix. In augmented coding you care about the code, its complexity, the tests, & their coverage. The value system in augmented coding is similar to hand coding--tidy code that works. It's just that I don't type much of that code.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Kent Beck reports good correctness and performance but poor code quality due to accidental complexity in the final augmented-coding result.
claims.quote: I feel good about the correctness & performance, not so good about the code quality. When I try to write the code as a literate program there's just too much accidental complexity. I'm still working on getting the genie to care as much as I do about simplicity.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: A warning sign that the AI agent was going off track was cheating by disabling or deleting tests.
claims.quote: Any indication that the genie was cheating, for example by disabling or deleting tests.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: In augmented coding, the human continuously watches intermediate agent output, intervenes to stop unproductive development, and checks whether the agent did the requested next test.
claims.quote: I watched the intermediate results of the genie more carefully, ready to intervene & stop unproductive development. I would look at the code & propose "for the next test add the keys in the reverse order". Then I'd look at the genie's work to see if it had done what I had asked.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Early augmented-coding attempts accumulated enough complexity that the agent stalled, forcing more human design intervention to keep the agent from coding ahead.
claims.quote: My first 2 attempts had accumulated so much complexity that the genie completely stalled. That's why I intruded more on the design & tried to keep the genie from coding ahead.
